To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have studied a large number of patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangectasia and found a large number of different mutations.

(1) ENG mutations are the most common cause of HHT in our Dutch HHT population; (2) HHT is a genetically heterogeneous disorder with a large number of mutations in ENG and ALK1; (3) the majority of the mutations are novel; and (4) there is a large variation in the severity of the disease in patients carrying the same mutation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the HHT population and with the identification of novel mutations in both genes, ENG and ALK1, in HHT patients.
the identification of new mutations and with the characterization of the genetic and molecular background of HHT.
the identification and characterization of mutations in the genes ENG and ALK1 in patients with HHT in the Netherlands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in 93% of the Dutch HHT families we identified mutations in ENG or ALK-1, and that in 7% of these families no mutation was found in the ENG or ALK 1 genes.
93% of the Dutch HHT families have mutations in either the ENG or ALK-1 genes, 7% have mutations in other genes and 1% has no mutations in either gene.
90% of HHT families have mutations in ENG or ALK-1, and in the other 10% of HHT patients, other genetic factors or environmental factors are responsible for HHT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HHT1 mutations are more prevalent in our Dutch HHT population than HHT2 mutations.
HHT is a genetically heterogeneous disorder, with a high frequency of mutations in the ENG gene.
93% of the HHT families in the Netherlands are caused by mutations in the ENG and/or ALK-1 genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HHT is genetically highly heterogeneous.
ENG and ALK1 are the main genes responsible for HHT.
ENG and ALK1 mutations are the major cause of HHT in the Netherlands.
